# computesphere_queue (Resource)

Manages a SphereQueue broker: a dedicated RabbitMQ message broker the platform runs for you. Pick an instance type (see the `computesphere_queue_instance_types` data source); the platform provisions it and generates its user and password. The password is never stored in Terraform state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    computesphere = {
      source  = "computesphere/computesphere"
      version = "~> 1.1"
    }
  }
}

variable "api_token" {
  description = "API token for ComputeSphere"
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "account_id" {
  description = "Account ID for ComputeSphere"
  type        = string
}

variable "api_url" {
  description = "API URL for ComputeSphere"
  type        = string
  default     = "api.computesphere.com"
}

provider "computesphere" {
  api_token  = var.api_token  # or set COMPUTESPHERE_API_TOKEN env variable
  account_id = var.account_id # or set COMPUTESPHERE_ACCOUNT_ID env variable
  api_url    = var.api_url    # or set COMPUTESPHERE_API_URL env variable
}

data "computesphere_queue_instance_types" "all" {
  environment_id = var.environment_id
}

resource "computesphere_queue" "example" {
  name           = "app-queue"
  environment_id = var.environment_id
  instance_type  = "sq-1c-2g-s20g" # Queue 1: 1 vCPU, 2 GB, 20 GB disk
}

variable "environment_id" {
  description = "Environment to create the broker in"
  type        = string
}

output "queue_id" {
  value = computesphere_queue.example.id
}

output "queue_members" {
  value = computesphere_queue.example.nodes
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) Environment the broker belongs to. Only services in this environment can reach it. It can't change after create; a change is refused at plan time.
- `instance_type` (String) Instance type id, e.g. `sq-1c-2g-s20g` (Queue 1). List them with the `computesphere_queue_instance_types` data source. A high-availability instance type (an id ending in `-ha`) runs three members across zones with quorum queues. Changing it resizes the broker in place; a size with less disk than the current one is refused.
- `name` (String) Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 40 characters; unique in the environment. It can't change after create; a change is refused at plan time.

### Optional

- `engine` (String) Broker engine. Only `rabbitmq` today. It can't change after create; a change is refused at plan time.
- `version` (String) RabbitMQ version, e.g. `4.3`. Defaults to the latest supported. It can't change after create; a change is refused at plan time.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `id` (String) Broker identifier.
- `nodes` (Number) Members of the broker's cluster: 1, or 3 on a high-availability instance type (an id ending in `-ha`).
- `project_id` (String) Project the broker belongs to.
- `region` (String) Region of the environment.
- `status` (String) Current status, e.g. `available`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to       = computesphere_queue.example
  identity = { id = "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890" }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String)

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = computesphere_queue.example
  id = "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a broker by its ID
terraform import computesphere_queue.example a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890
```
